article_title: The Effect of Authentic Learning Approach in Social Studies Teaching on the Academic Success
citation: Fitnat Gürgil. (2018). The Effect of Authentic Learning Approach in Social Studies Teaching on the Academic Success. Universal Journal of Educational Research 6(10): 2061-2068. https://doi.org/10.13189/ujer.2018.061002
title: 30-item researcher-developed academic achievement test (KR-20 = .83)
description: A data collection tool built from a literature review of the 'Production, Distribution and Consumption' unit. A 40-question draft was reviewed by two social studies lecturers, one assessment-and-evaluation lecturer and two teachers; 4 questions were removed and 3 adjusted. After piloting with 213 students and item analysis, "30 items with a KR  20 reliability coefficient of .83 were included in the achievement test." Difficulty and discriminability indices were calculated for each item, and six unsuitable items were removed.
requirements: Expert review by subject and assessment specialists
Item analysis of difficulty and discriminability indices before final use
constraints: Validated only for the 'Production, Distribution and Consumption' unit of 5th-grade social studies
target_learning_goals: Social studies content knowledge in the production, distribution and consumption unit
examples: The test was piloted on 213 students from three schools of low, medium and high socioeconomic characteristics before use as pretest and posttest
key_sources: Fitnat Gürgil. (2018). The Effect of Authentic Learning Approach in Social Studies Teaching on the Academic Success. Universal Journal of Educational Research 6(10): 2061-2068. https://doi.org/10.13189/ujer.2018.061002

article_title: Enhancing medical students' diagnostic accuracy of infectious keratitis with AI-generated images.
citation: Xie Wenjia, Yuan Zhouhang, Si Yuxuan, Huang Zhengxing, Li Yingming, Wu Fei, Yao Yu-Feng. (2025). Enhancing medical students’ diagnostic accuracy of infectious keratitis with AI-generated images. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07592-y
title: 30-question image-based diagnostic test for infectious keratitis
description: A diagnostic test assessing students' ability to diagnose infectious keratitis before and after teaching. "The test consisted of 30 single-choice questions, with an equal distribution across three categories: bacterial, fungal, and herpes simplex keratitis, each represented by 10 questions." Each question presented a slit-lamp photograph from a real patient not appearing in any group's teaching, with three diagnostic options; the same question set was administered before and after teaching, and accuracy (proportion of true results among total cases) served as the outcome measure.
requirements: Test images are real patient photographs that did not appear in any group's teaching process
constraints: Students were unaware of the proportion of questions per disease type; the same question set was reused pre and post
target_learning_goals: differential diagnosis of bacterial, fungal, and viral keratitis from corneal images
examples: The same 30-question test was administered before and after the teaching session to all three groups
key_sources: Xie Wenjia, Yuan Zhouhang, Si Yuxuan, Huang Zhengxing, Li Yingming, Wu Fei, Yao Yu-Feng. (2025). Enhancing medical students’ diagnostic accuracy of infectious keratitis with AI-generated images. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07592-y
